newsitem.title: EGYPT: Bargain hunting supports Egyptian shares.
newsitem.headline: Bargain hunting supports Egyptian shares.

text.p: Egyptian share prices found strong support on Tuesday as bargain hunters stepped in to buy stocks hard hit in the correction of the previous week.
The Capital Market Authority's all-share index rose 6.80 points to close at 400.54, from 393.74 points on Monday. Turnover was an average 73.93 million pounds ($21.8 million).
"It's too soon to say the correction is fully over but there is demand for shares that went very cheap in the recent fall, especially mills," said Sherif Cararah of brokers EFG-Hermes.
Cararah predicted that the market could stagnate or slip again during the month but would make a strong recovery later in March when new funds start investing in the Egyptian market.
On Tuesday the milling and cement sectors both did well, with few exceptions, but banks continued mixed.

"Banks are seeing some support at this level but I don't see it staying for long. They are the most expensive stocks in the market, though there is the argument that their profit margins are going to increase," Cararah said.

Commercial International Bank (CIB), was the most active stock with nearly nine million pounds turnover. It put on 40 pounds to 900 but it is still sharply down on the record high of 1,020 reached on February 25.
The second most active share was Abu Qir Fertilisers and Chemical Industries, which rose 5.00 to close at 106.00 in trade worth 8.940 million pounds, the CMA said.
In the milling sector, North Cairo Flour Mills added 2.00 pounds to end at 188.00, still well down on the all-time highs it hit in February.
Related company General Silos and Storage jumped back the session maximum of five percent for the second day running, closing at 116.44 pounds.
The main exception in the sector was South Cairo Flour Mills, which Cararah said was the least liquid of the mills.
Suez Cement and Amriyah Cement both caught the upturn but Helwan Portland Cement slipped a fraction to 79.99 pounds.
Misr International Bank, the probable target of a global depositary receipt offering, fell 40.10 to 767.89.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 652.15 from 635.08 points on Monday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms was also up, at 268.25 from 265.32.
Out of the 89 shares traded, 45 gained, 22 lost and 22 ended the day unchanged.
